## Context / Problem

S1 (`filmable-crushing-nighthawk`, `src/rebar/_commands/reclaim_collapse.py:63` `collapse_shadow_tracker`) produces a rewritten below-horizon baseline in a disposable shadow clone. This story builds the **publish-swap** that would replace the published `tickets` history with that baseline, and the **rollback** that would restore it, both behind one precondition: replace only if the remote is unchanged since T0, else abort with no write. ADR 0106 §6 (`docs/adr/0106-remote-anchored-history-reclamation.md:126-135`) requires a git-ref CAS on git remotes and an exclusive bundle-set replacement on the `git-remote-s3` backend, because the S3 auto-doctor (`src/rebar/_store/s3_doctor.py:62` `heal_multi_bundle`) folds divergent heads into a lossless merge and would resurrect the replaced history. Nothing executes a real swap here; the S3 dry-run story and a human go/no-go drive it later.

## Approach

One new library module, `src/rebar/_commands/reclaim_publish.py`, with no CLI verb (the S3 dry-run harness is its only caller). Every entry point first calls S1's shadow guard `_assert_shadow_tracker` (`reclaim_collapse.py:200`), which refuses anything without the `.rebar/reclaim-shadow-clone` marker, with a configured remote, or equal to the live tracker. Pushes go to an explicit remote URL argument, so the shadow never needs a named remote.

- **Epoch stamp.** `stamp_superseding_epoch(shadow, new_epoch, replaced_tip="HEAD")` commits, on the shadow's HEAD, the store-compat record of `replaced_tip` re-stamped with `compat.superseding_record` (`src/rebar/_store/compat.py:291`, merged with `sarcastic-specified-kodiakbear` in 9099c548247). Clones on the replaced history then prove supersession through `compat.remote_epoch_supersedes_local` and take the stale-clone override in `src/rebar/_store/stale_override.py`.
- **git ref remotes** (bare, GitHub, Gerrit): `publish_git_ref` runs ONE `git push --atomic --force-with-lease=refs/heads/<branch>:<T0> <url> <new>:refs/heads/<branch> <T0>:refs/tickets-backup/pre-reclaim-<stamp>`. The same push creates the backup ref at T0 and moves the branch; a moved branch fails the lease and the atomic push writes neither ref (`PublishAborted`).
- **S3** (`git-remote-s3`, ADR 0093): `publish_s3_bundle_set` takes the helper's per-ref lock (`acquire_lock`, as `s3_doctor.heal_multi_bundle` does), asserts the bundle-head set (`get_bundles_for_ref`, sha from the key) equals the T0 set or aborts, copies every original bundle to `<prefix>/<ref>/PROTECTED#rollback-<stamp>/` (keys the helper's enumeration already skips), writes one bundle of the new tip, deletes the originals, calls `init_remote_head`, and releases the lock in `finally`. The doctor is never called.
- **Rollback re-convergence.** `rollback_git_ref` publishes a restored tip under a lease on the rewritten tip. The restored tip is the backup tip plus a stamp with `replaced_tip=<rewritten tip>`, so its lineage names both the original and the rewritten epochs. Clients already on the rewritten baseline see unrelated history with a superseding epoch and are overridden back (aff9's protocol). Clients that never moved share history with the restored tip; for them `compat.store_epoch_problem` (`compat.py:200`) is relaxed to allow the union when the remote lineage names the local epoch, so their unpushed writes merge instead of being refused.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_commands/reclaim_publish.py` (new): stamp, git-ref publish, git-ref rollback, S3 bundle-set publish.
- `src/rebar/_store/compat.py`: `store_epoch_problem` accepts a remote whose lineage names the local epoch.
- `tests/unit/test_reclaim_publish.py` (new): git-ref adapter and rollback re-convergence against throwaway bare remotes.
- `tests/integration/test_reclaim_publish_s3.py` (new): S3 adapter against `tests/integration/s3_doctor_harness.py`'s `FakeS3Remote`.
- `docs/concurrency.md`: a short "Publishing a reclaimed baseline" paragraph next to aff9's reconnect protocol.

## Testing

TDD, red first; all repositories are throwaways under `tmp_path`, S3 is the fake.

- git ref happy path: branch moves to the new tip and `refs/tickets-backup/pre-reclaim-*` holds T0.
- git ref failure: a writer pushes after T0; the swap raises `PublishAborted` and the remote branch and backup namespace are unchanged.
- Shadow guard: a plain clone (no marker) is refused.
- Rollback: a client that moved onto the rewritten baseline is overridden back onto the restored tip; a client that never moved keeps its unpushed event merged on top of the restored tip; a rollback whose lease is stale aborts with no write.
- S3 happy path: exactly one bundle remains and clones to the new tip; each original's bytes exist under the rollback prefix; the lock is released.
- S3 failures: a head set different from T0 aborts with the object directory byte-for-byte unchanged; a held lock aborts with no write.
- Doctor bypass: running `heal_multi_bundle` after the swap is a `noop` and T0 is unreachable from the published tip.
- `pytest tests/integration/test_reclaim_publish_s3.py -m integration` is run explicitly in addition to `make verify` (whose integration tier also selects it).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The git-ref adapter swaps via `--force-with-lease` and aborts with no write when the remote moved since T0, verified on a throwaway bare remote by `tests/unit/test_reclaim_publish.py`.
- [ ] The S3 adapter performs a push-locked bundle-set replacement that asserts the T0 head set, backs up bundles to a rollback prefix, writes one rewritten bundle, deletes the originals, and is not merged back by the auto-doctor, verified on the fake-S3 fixture by `tests/integration/test_reclaim_publish_s3.py`.
- [ ] A backup ref (git) or rollback bundle prefix (S3) is captured before the first destructive step in each adapter, asserted by the same tests.
- [ ] The rollback re-convergence path is documented in `docs/concurrency.md` and covered by a fixture in which a client on the rewritten baseline is overridden back onto the restored ref.
- [ ] `make verify` is run and any failure is fixed or shown environmental (it passes when rerun in isolation or outside the agent sandbox); the Gerrit change gets `Verified +1`; `python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` and `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` exit 0.
- [ ] [non-codebase] No real `tickets` remote is swapped by this story; all evidence comes from `tmp_path` repositories and the fake S3 remote.
  provenance: environment=developer workstation worktree plus Gerrit CI; principal=RebarBotNava agent session rebar-session-3d705fec; privilege_posture=no write access used against the shared tickets branch beyond normal MCP tracker events; instrument=code inspection of the merged change (every swap and push targets a tmp_path repository or the fake S3 remote) — justification: the story adds library code and tests only, and no swap is executed against any real store.

## Portability

Both adapters use core-git ref primitives (`push --atomic --force-with-lease`, `bundle create`) or the store's existing `git-remote-s3` seam; nothing depends on a CI provider.
